sections.title: Timed phone journey and analytics
sections.what: Runs the main loop on a phone-sized screen, requires it to finish within sixty seconds without sideways scrolling, and checks the expected analytics events were recorded for that user.
sections.why: Protects the speed and mobile fit of the core experience, and confirms usage tracking works.
sections.watch_out: The sixty-second limit and exact event list are both strict, so slow runs or analytics changes will fail it.

summary: A timed browser test of the main user journey on a phone-sized screen: view a moment, lock a call, review it, and move to the next moment, with analytics events checked in the database.
purpose: Checks the core loop is fast, does not scroll sideways on a phone, and records the expected usage events.
why: The product promises a quick loop on mobile, and the analytics events feed the product team's view of usage.
how: It creates a user and signs in on a 390 pixel wide phone viewport. It starts a timer, opens the first moment, locks a call at the second option, opens the review, then moves to the next read. It stops the timer, records the time as an annotation, and expects it under sixty seconds. It checks the page does not scroll sideways, then queries the database for that user's analytics events and expects a specific sorted list including two view events and the lock and grade events.
inputs: A new user, the phone viewport, and the database records for that user.
outputs: Pass or fail, plus a timing annotation for the run.
risks: The timing check can fail on a slow machine even when the app is correct. The exact event list will break whenever analytics changes.
debug: If it is slow, check the timing annotation and the slowest step. If events are missing, check that each user action fires its analytics event.
